CALLER STATED SOMEONE FROM A NEIGHBORING COMPANY REPORTED A RELEASE OF VAPOR TO THE AIR ON 07-JUL-2010 TO THE MIAMI-DADE FIRE DEPARTMENT. CALLER STATED THEIR OWN EMPLOYEES SMELLED A LINGERING ODOR OF ANHYDROUS AMMONIA ON 05-JUL-2010 IN EVENING GOING INTO 06-JUL-2010 MORNING BUT NOTHING WAS REPORTED. THE EMPLOYEES WERE NOT AFFECTED BY THE ODOR VAPORS DURING THE EVENING TO MORNING SHIFT AT THE FACILITY.

AT APPROXIMATELY 0900 HRS. MARINA STAFF OBSERVED A THIN RAINBOW SHEEN IN THE WATER AT THE BOW OF THE 86' FISHING TENDER EIGIL B., EXTENDING 50' FROM IT, THEN POOLING IN AN AREA APPROXIMATELY 50' X 30'. MARINA STAFF MADE THE OBSERVATION FROM PIER A, WHILE THE VESSEL WAS ANCHORED ABOUT 150' AWAY. ANOTHER VESSEL, A U.S. NAVY TUG, SKENANDOA WAS ANCHORED NEARBY. PIER A IS A LARGE 300' LONG ELEVATED COMMERCIAL PIER. MARINA STAFF REPORTED THAT THE SHEEN APPEARED TO BE COMING FROM THE EIGIL B. AND NOT FROM THE SKENANDOA. MARINA STAFF HAD A REASONABLE SUSPICION TO BELIEVE THAT THE EIGIL B. WAS THE SOURCE OF THE SHEEN BUT COULD NOT VERIFY IT. MARINA OFFICE STAFF PHONED THE OWNER/OPERATOR AND INQUIRED ABOUT THE SHEEN. THEY STATED IN SUBSTANCE, ONLY, THAT THERE WAS ANOTHER VESSEL NEARBY. THEY STATED THAT THEY WERE UNDER WAY AND HAD DEPARTED THE MARINA. MARINA STAFF REPORTED THAT WHEN THE EIGIL B.
